The Australian government has raised the HELP repayment threshold to $67,000 and shifted to a marginal repayment system, aiming to ease the cost-of-living pressure on graduates.

The Poison:
The extended duration of debt means more interest is accrued over time, potentially leaving some graduates in a cycle of debt longer than under the previous system.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
There is no plane error; the article accurately balances the immediate benefit against the long-term mathematical reality of the loan.

Social Physics Analysis:
By shifting to a marginal system, the government empowers lower earners to manage their cash flow, demonstrating a transparent approach to social policy.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. The policy aligns intent with measurable relief.

The Unavoidable Truth: Lower monthly repayments provide immediate relief for cost-of-living pressures.

The Unavoidable Lie: The total cost of the loan remains unchanged despite the new repayment structure.
